clue.text: Ray, perhaps, not entirely mean to eat morsel of food, a scrap

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a ray is an example of a fish

indicators.note: the stingy word swallows a letter, so it holds it inside

parts.note: a mean person is tight with money

indicators.note: only a small bite, the opening letter, is taken from the word

explanation.surface: A ray, the fish, being stingy about eating a scrap of food it was offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray, perhaps' is a definition by example. 'scrap' looks like a crumb going with the food, but it means a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a slang word for a punch-up, a brawl with bare knuckles.

clue.text: Succeed, like something powdery?

parts.note: flour is a fine milled powder
the suffix -ish means like or resembling

explanation.surface: Asking whether success is like being made of powder.
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix comes after the powder in the answer though 'like' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed in life is to thrive or prosper, growing well.

clue.text: Biblical city like this, with kind of effect half erased

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

indicators.note: the second half of the word is rubbed out, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: the domino effect is a chain reaction

explanation.surface: Describing an ancient city with a special effect partly wiped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half erased' takes INO off DOMINO, leaving DOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament city destroyed by fire and brimstone alongside Gomorrah.

clue.text: Pink organ inelastic, if man excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A body part that is pink and unstretchy, if a man is aroused: a risqué picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges INELASTIC, IF and MAN. 'Organ' here means a publication, and this British business daily is famously printed on pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper, and the London business paper is known for its salmon-pink pages.

clue.text: Climbing back into pig monster

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the whole is read from bottom to top
the rear part goes inside the swine word

parts.note: a hog is a pig
a tail is at the back of an animal

explanation.surface: Something clambering onto a pig's back to reveal a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts TAIL in HOG to give HTAILOG; 'Climbing' turns all of it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine giant slain by David is a byword for a huge, monstrous figure.

clue.text: Tiny thing bagged for a nicker?

definitions.text: Tiny thing bagged for a nicker?

parts.words: Tiny thing bagged for a nicker?
parts.note: a small flake of tea sealed in a teabag; in cockney rhyming slang the phrase also means thief, a nicker being someone who nicks things

explanation.surface: Something small packed in a bag for a pound coin (a nicker is British slang for a pound).
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang uses the phrase for 'thief'; 'nicker' hides 'one who nicks', not the slang pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for thief, and literally a scrap of tea found in a teabag.

clue.text: Fraud no PCs will back

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Apple Macs are computers that are not PCs

explanation.surface: A con trick that no police constables will support.
explanation.walkthrough: PCs looks like police constables but means personal computers, so 'no PCs' is MACS; 'will back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or con is a dishonest trick to cheat someone.

clue.text: Vital force left out of dance, doubly for ankle-biter

parts.note: chi is the life energy of Chinese philosophy

indicators.note: the shortened dance word is written twice
the letter is dropped out of the dance word

parts.note: the hula is a Hawaiian dance

explanation.surface: Energy drained from a dance twice over makes for a nippy pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes L from HULA to give HUA; 'doubly' repeats it. An ankle-biter is a small yappy dog (also slang for a child).
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny Mexican breed of dog is the classic small yapping animal that nips at ankles.

clue.text: Chaos, with one of twelve on the brink

parts.note: May is one of the twelve months
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: Chaos, with one of the twelve apostles on the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe wild disorder and confusion.

clue.text: Flit suggested — so take flight, then?

parts.note: the word flit is the letters of lift jumbled, so it is suggested by those letters put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Moving out is hinted at, so leave by flying away.
explanation.walkthrough: A broken lift means you must take a flight of stairs: 'flight' is the staircase, not flying.
explanation.definitionFit: When the elevator is broken you climb the staircase, that is, take a flight of steps.

clue.text: Ancient, somewhat wizened looking from the rear

indicators.note: the run is read starting at its back end
only some of the letters of these words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Someone very old, a bit shrivelled when seen from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes NEDLO from wizeNED LOoking; 'from the rear' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an archaic word for times long past, of old.

clue.text: Debt of £1 on gift

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, stands for the pound
the Roman numeral for one
a gift is a talent or ability

explanation.surface: A one-pound debt on a present.
explanation.definitionFit: On a balance sheet a debt owed is recorded as an obligation to pay.

clue.text: God welcoming national state

indicators.note: the god takes the citizen in, holding it inside

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
an Omani is a national of Oman

explanation.surface: A deity receiving a citizen of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan country in eastern Europe, a nation state.

clue.text: Force out old terrorist leader, boorish

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter of the word

parts.note: boorish manners are rude

explanation.surface: Expel an old terrorist chief who is uncouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to push or squeeze something out through an opening.

clue.text: Fair to wash hand

parts.note: a fair deal is straight, honest
to flush is to wash out with water

explanation.surface: Fair to go and wash one's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' is a poker hand: five cards in sequence all of one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker a run of five consecutive cards of one suit is one of the best holdings.

clue.text: Bad manners with old twins a prominent feature

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are badly arranged, mixed up

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old, and twins gives two of it

explanation.surface: Poor manners in an elderly pair of twins stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges MANNERS with OO.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquiline nose with a high bridge is a striking facial feature.

clue.text: Ask Dickensian to feel resentment

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Asking a Dickens character to feel bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: To grudge something to someone is to resent giving or allowing it.

clue.text: Drink in hemlock, it's poisonous as sweet

indicators.note: the drink goes inside the jumbled letters
poisonous suggests something corrupted, so these letters are mangled

parts.note: the 's is the verb is, so only the two letters count
cola is a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: A drink laced with hemlock is poisonous, though sweet to taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poisonous' is the anagram signal, not a description of the drink; 'sweet' is the British word for a piece of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of the creamy confection is a sweet, a British word for candy.

clue.text: Vehicle in which cups and saucers might be thrown around?

definitions.text: Vehicle in which cups and saucers might be thrown around?

parts.words: Vehicle in which cups and saucers might be thrown around?
parts.note: split as cha, slang for tea, and riot, a mêlée where crockery might fly

explanation.surface: A wagon in which crockery gets thrown about on a bumpy ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as CHA RIOT: a 'tea riot' is where cups and saucers would fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle from ancient racing and warfare.

clue.text: Maybe second test outlines racket?

indicators.note: the test word surrounds the noise word, outlining it

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: Perhaps a second test of a tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Second is an example of a number showing position in a sequence, like first or third.

clue.text: Wildcat taking drink is naughty

parts.note: wild says the letters of cat are rearranged
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A wildcat lapping up a drink is misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Wildcat' as 'wild cat': CAT rearranged makes ACT, which then takes SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly, misbehave.

clue.text: Frank, a cause of irritation

parts.note: frank means candid, outspoken

explanation.surface: Frank is an irritant: a man described as a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeast fungus behind thrush is a common source of itching.

clue.text: Cap removed from element by GP, one releases medicine

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a doctor

indicators.note: the top letter is taken off the word

parts.note: copper is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A doctor releasing medicine after removing a cap from an element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap removed from' takes C off COPPER, leaving OPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipette lets out liquid medicine one drop at a time.

clue.text: Second fruit? Exactly

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
B is second in the alphabet and the second grade

explanation.surface: A query about a second piece of fruit, answered exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb means precisely, as in plumb in the middle.

clue.text: Reversible fasteners pinning baker, European

indicators.note: the fasteners hold the baker in their middle
the word can be read backwards

parts.note: nails fasten things
an oven bakes

explanation.surface: Fasteners pinning down a baker from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible' gives SLIAN. Baker is the appliance that bakes, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Slovenia is a European, from a country on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Priest managed to screen scrummy entertainment?

indicators.note: the word screens, hides, the other inside it

parts.note: did means managed, coped
RU is rugby union, a sport with scrums

explanation.surface: A clergyman managed to show some delicious entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrummy' looks like 'delicious', but points to the rugby scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Druids were priests of the ancient Celtic religion.

clue.text: Look to get sound from woofer

indicators.note: the word for the dog is said aloud

parts.note: a peke is a Pekinese dog, a woofer

explanation.surface: Listening to the noise from a loudspeaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A woofer is a bass speaker, but here a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick glance, a brief look.

clue.text: List including unlimited dance music, OK

indicators.note: the list takes the dance inside it

parts.note: a table is a list of data

indicators.note: the outer letters are removed, its limits taken away

parts.note: Ravel's Bolero is dance music

explanation.surface: A playlist featuring endless dance music, which is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips B and O from BOLERO, leaving OLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tolerable is acceptable, passable, all right.
